symptoms: Concentric dark rings (target spot appearance) on lower, older leaves.
Yellow halo surrounding brownish-black leaf spots.
Premature leaf loss starting from bottom foliage progressing upward.
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungal infection (Alternaria solani) favoured by humid weather, warm temperatures (24-29°C), and wet foliage.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove severely infected lower leaves immediately. Apply copper-based fungicide or Mancozeb every 7-10 days. Ensure drip irrigation instead of overhead watering to keep leaves dry.
Tomato___Early_blight.fertilizer: Apply balanced N-P-K (19-19-19) with calcium nitrate spray to strengthen plant cell walls and promote fresh foliage growth.
prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Mulch around base of plant to prevent soil spores splashing onto leaves.
Maintain proper plant spacing (45-60cm) for adequate airflow.

symptoms: Large water-soaked lesions turning dark brown to black on leaf tips and margins.
White fungal growth on leaf undersides under high humidity.
Rapid wilting and blighting of entire foliage.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete pathogen (Phytophthora infestans) spreading rapidly during cool, wet conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Destroy infected plants immediately to stop spread. Apply systemic protective fungicide at early stage.
Potato___Late_blight.fertilizer: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers. Apply potash to increase resistance.
prevention: Ensure proper soil ridging around plants.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with no spotting, discoloration, or lesions.
Sturdy stem and normal leaf growth pattern.
Tomato___Healthy.cause: Optimal growing conditions and good crop management.
Tomato___Healthy.treatment: No treatment required. Maintain current care routine.
Tomato___Healthy.fertilizer: Continue regular balanced fertilization schedule according to growth stage.
prevention: Monitor regularly for early signs of pests or pathogens.
Maintain proper soil moisture and nutrient levels.
